From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: Renewal + Two-Phase Throughput Uplift — lock QBR window

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our call, I wanted to kick off the renewal conversation and outline the two-phase throughput uplift path we discussed (short summary below), confirm stakeholders, and lock a QBR slot to make decisions and align on procurement timing.

Quick summary (proposal):
- Phase 1 (Q3 start): 1.5x committed throughput for predictable traffic surges; 6-month term amendment.
- Phase 2 (Q4–Q1): optional staircase to 2.5x with seasonal burst lanes and reserved headroom; requires exec sign-off and CAPEX timeline.

Stakeholders I have on our side: me (AM), Marissa (Renewals lead), Karthik (Solutions / capacity sizing). Please confirm your review team — I have Alex (you) and Contracts on the thread for now.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick QBR to review MAP and finalize timeline — proposed windows attached (QBR_slots.ics).
2) I’ll drop a mutual action plan draft to the Drive and send to Contracts after your sign-off.
3) Technical sizing session with Karthik if you want to validate burst headroom assumptions.

Attachments: StratusAI_MAP_v1.xlsx (draft mutual action plan), QBR_slots.ics (proposed three windows).

Can you confirm who else from Stratus should be involved (finance/procurement/infra) and which QBR window works best? If none of the three slots work, we’ll expand availability next week.

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124
Redwood Inference

Vanessa —

Appreciate the clear plan. This matches internal goals. Quick answers:
- I’m looping in our Head of Infrastructure (Lena Cho) and Procurement (contracts@stratusai.com) — copied above.
- Of the three slots, Friday 14 Jun (slot 2) looks best for our exec and infra leads.
- We’d like the MAP to include a simple cost delta table by month (total and per-token estimates) and any required lead time for Phase 2 (GPU procurement / reserved capacity).

Can Marissa and Karthik confirm the lead time assumptions? Also, we have a pending budget review the week after the QBR — if we can have a contractual framing + redline-ready amendment within 10 business days after the QBR, that would help stitching approvals.

Thanks,

Alex / Vanessa / team —

Quick update from Renewals:
- We reviewed proposed term amendment templates and can prepare a 6-month amendment for Phase 1 and a bilateral option addendum for Phase 2.
- Confirmed internal SLA targets for Phase 1 (same latency SLO; increased burst quota).
- Cost delta: I’ll attach a short worksheet to the MAP by EOD Friday with month-by-month estimates and how we amortize any reserved capacity.

Karthik — can you confirm lead times for the reserved GPU profile we recommended and a short bullet on the operational impact (KV cache changes, autoscaling ramp)?

Alex — we can commit to preparing a redline-ready amendment within 8–10 business days after the QBR if procurement receives the MAP and cost worksheet at or before the QBR. That should meet your budget review timing.

Next actions:
- Vanessa: send final MAP + cost worksheet into Drive before the QBR; move the QBR invite to Fri 14 Jun if Alex confirms.
- Karthik: technical sizing note by EOD Thu.
- Alex / Contracts: confirm attendee list (esp. finance contact) by EOD Thu so we can route the amendment correctly.

Alex / team —

Technical sizing note (short):
- Reserved GPU lead time: 4–6 weeks for the specific Ampere-class pool we recommend; Phase 1 can be supported immediately with existing burst lanes and autoscaling (no hardware purchases required).
- Operational impact: Phase 1 uses prefix/KV cache tuning and adjusted batching parameters; expected increase in per-token throughput with minor config changes and a single technical runbook. Phase 2 will require capacity reservation and an ops runbook for traffic shaping (we estimate 2 full runbook days for playbook validation).
- Risk & mitigation: the primary risk is transient tail-latency during the initial ramp; mitigate with canary routing and a 48-hour staged rollout.

Vanessa / Marissa: I’ll upload a one-page tech appendix to the MAP and add the lead-time bullet.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
